thread.title: RelayOps Audit Assistant content launch planning

plannerRecommendationGate.unlockBehavior: Advance to task_mapping and recommend Generate Tasks from Chat only after the launch brief and KPI target are explicit.

content: We are launching Audit Assistant in early May and need one coherent eight-week content engine instead of scattered asset requests.
The launch brief, brand messaging framework, and ICP interview notes are uploaded.
I want this plan to work for marketing execution and for sales follow-up, not just for SEO.
The launch brief and messaging framework already support a clear operations-led narrative, and the interview notes confirm that scramble and ownership confusion are the main pains.
Before I can recommend task generation, I still need the KPI target to be explicit and I need confirmation that the content window truly runs across late April through mid June.
Please confirm the success metric and any channel-performance constraints.
Use 45 assisted demo requests as the primary KPI for the eight-week window from 2026-04-20 through 2026-06-12.
Webinars and operational blog content performed best, and sales wants the plan to address the spreadsheet and ROI objections directly.
SEO should focus on audit readiness, evidence workflow, and leadership visibility rather than generic compliance checklist content.
You now have enough business signal to move into blueprint.

The primary audience is an operations leader at a mid-market company with recurring audit pressure, and the message should center on moving from scramble-based prep to always-ready operations without adding headcount.
The best launch spine is messaging matrix -> topic clusters -> editorial calendar -> three flagship briefs -> channel distribution -> KPI tracker.
visionUpdate: - Primary buyer: Director or Senior Manager of Operations
- Secondary influences: Compliance manager, operations systems lead, sales champion
- Primary message: move from reactive audit prep to always-ready compliance operations without adding headcount
- Proof pillars: evidence visibility, readiness accountability, leadership confidence
- Prioritize audit readiness, evidence workflow, and leadership visibility clusters
- Reuse webinar-friendly content because webinar performance is strong
- Ensure the content briefs directly address spreadsheet and ROI objections

content: The blueprint is right, but keep the production load realistic: one major asset per week plus repurposing.
I also want the sales objection coverage to show up in the briefs, not just in the messaging matrix.
If that is reflected, I want to move to task mapping.
The plan is specific enough to enter task mapping.

Generate Tasks from Chat should now produce seven tasks: define audience and KPI, approve the messaging matrix, select topic clusters, build the editorial calendar, draft three briefs, create the distribution checklist, and define the KPI tracker.
The representative review gate should sit on the content-brief task, because that is where the scenario proves that planning outputs became execution-ready assets.
recommendedGeneratedTasks: Define target audience and launch success metrics
Select topic clusters and SEO priorities
Create the distribution checklist by channel
Define KPI tracker and reporting cadence

content: The seven tasks are generated.
Please tighten the KPI task so it explicitly covers source systems and the weekly reporting cadence.
Leave the title alone; I only want the description refined.
Agreed. The KPI task should stay focused on metric definitions, data sources, ownership, and the Monday reporting rhythm.
I am proposing one task mutation that updates the existing KPI task description without changing the task title.

fields.description: Define the KPI tracker, source systems, owners, and weekly reporting cadence for the eight-week content engine.

taskGenerationRecommendation.notes: The planner recommendation is the gate. The scenario does not invent a separate board-lock API.
